policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'I wrote for him' permits both the qere and ketiv spellings of the same first-person verb and supplies no mapped textual note distinguishing them; retain the qere base fallback.
ASV 'the ten thousand things of my law' renders the qere רֻבֵּי as a construct expression of multiplicity, distinguishing it from the ketiv רבו.
